content:
The Fractions & Decimals chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Fractions & Decimals tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Fractions & Decimals

Operations on fractions, comparing fractions, and terminating vs recurring decimals.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Add/subtract via the LCM of denominators; divide by multiplying by the reciprocal.
  • A fraction terminates iff its reduced denominator has only 2s and 5s.
  • Pure recurring 0.ā = a/9; a k-digit block over 99…9.
  • Compare by cross-multiplying or converting to decimals.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Adding numerators and denominators separately.
  • Not reducing before testing for a terminating decimal.
  • Decimal-point slips in multiplication.

faq.q: When does a fraction give a terminating decimal?
faq.a: When, in lowest terms, the denominator has only the prime factors 2 and 5.

faq.q: How to convert a recurring decimal to a fraction?
faq.a: Put the repeating block over as many 9s as its length (e.g. 0.′45′ = 45/99 = 5/11).
